directAnswer: You can check if your password has been leaked by using online services like Have I Been Pwned or by enabling alerts from your password manager.
summary: Password leaks can compromise your security. Regularly checking if your credentials have been exposed is essential.

sections.heading: What is a Password Leak?
sections.body: A password leak occurs when your credentials are exposed in a data breach, making them available to malicious actors.

sections.heading: How to Check for Leaked Passwords
sections.body: Utilize online tools and services that aggregate data from known breaches to see if your password has been compromised.

sections.heading: Preventive Measures
sections.body: Consider using a password manager and enabling two-factor authentication to enhance your security.

steps.title: Use Have I Been Pwned
steps.detail: Visit the Have I Been Pwned website, enter your email address, and check for any breaches associated with your account.

steps.title: Check with Your Password Manager
steps.detail: If you use a password manager, check its security dashboard for any alerts regarding compromised passwords.

steps.title: Enable Alerts
steps.detail: Set up alerts for any future breaches related to your accounts through services like Google or your password manager.

faqs.question: What should I do if my password has been leaked?
faqs.answer: Immediately change your password and enable two-factor authentication on your accounts.

faqs.question: Can I recover my account if my password was leaked?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically you can recover your account by resetting your password using the recovery options provided by the service.

faqs.question: Are there any tools that can help me monitor my passwords?
faqs.answer: Yes, password managers like LastPass and 1Password offer monitoring features that alert you to compromised passwords.

caveats: Not all breaches are reported immediately, so it's advisable to check regularly.
